transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's nice to meet you too. Thank you for fitting me in. I, um... I hope I'm not wasting your time, because it's probably just normal stress, but... I came in because I just keep beating myself up lately. 

I've been having this feeling that I'm not really, you know, senior material at work. I'm a systems analyst, and recently I just can't shake the thought that I've somehow fooled everyone into thinking I could handle way more than I actually can. It sounds a little silly saying it out loud, I know, and I really don't want to complain when I have a good job... but it's just been weighing on me. Is that... is that the right kind of thing to talk about here?
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Well, um... I don't know if "depressed" is too strong a word. I really don't want to sound like I'm whining, because I know people have it much worse, you know? But... I guess, yeah, most days lately I've just had this... this heavy, low feeling. It's sort of like I'm just moving through my day at work and at home, but the color is just... turned down? If that makes sense. 

I'm sorry, I hope that's not a weird way to describe it. Does that sound like what you're asking about?
Do these feelings seem mainly connected to stress at work?

Um, well... I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I hope it's okay that I don't have a very clear answer for that. I mean, work can be a lot sometimes, but... I really don't want to blame my job, because it's a good place and they've been very fair to me. 

And honestly, I still get that heavy feeling even on the weekends when I'm not looking at any systems or thinking about the office at all. So I guess... maybe it's not just work? I'm sorry, I wish I could give you a better explanation. Is it normal to not really know exactly where it's coming from?
Have you been enjoying things less than usual lately?

Well, um... I guess so. I mean, I don't want to sound ungrateful for the free time I have, but... yeah. Usually, I really look forward to the weekends. I like to grill out, or maybe go fishing, or even just sit down and put on a good record. 

But lately... I don't know, I just sort of leave all my gear sitting there. I'll look at the grill and just think, "Why bother?" and I don't really care about doing any of it. It's probably just a phase, right? I'm sure I'll get back into it soon. I hope it's not too unusual to just... lose the drive for your hobbies like that?
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living?

Oh, um... gosh. I really don't want to alarm you, or make it sound worse than it is. I definitely haven't made any sort of plan to hurt myself or anything like that. I know I have a lot to be grateful for, and I would never want to do that to the people around me. 

But... well, I guess I do catch myself sometimes just thinking that... maybe it would be easier if I just didn't wake up some morning? Just to not have to push through that heavy feeling anymore. 

I'm so sorry, I know that probably sounds terrible to say out loud. I really don't mean to sound dramatic or ungrateful for my life. Is it... is it somewhat common for people to have thoughts like that when they get in these slumps? I hope you don't think less of me for admitting that.
How long have you been feeling this heavy, low mood?

Well, um... I guess if I really sit down and trace it back... I hope it's okay that I let it go on this long without saying anything. I just kept thinking I could snap myself out of it, you know? I didn't want to be a bother. 

But looking back, these... these low periods, where I just feel so guilty and heavy... they've been hanging around, off and on, for about eleven months now. I know I probably should have come in sooner. I'm sorry for waiting so long. I just really wanted to believe I was handling it fine on my own. Does that make sense? I hope I didn't let things get too far out of hand before asking for help.
During the past 11 months, have there been at least 2 weeks in a row when you felt down nearly every day?

Well, um... yeah, I suppose so. I really hope I'm not making it sound like I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself all the time. I still go to work and do what I need to do. But... yeah, definitely for at least two weeks at a time, probably longer, honestly. 

Most days lately, I've just had this... this heavy, low feeling. It's almost like I'm just moving through my day, going to work, coming home, but... the color is just turned down on everything, if that makes sense? I'm still functioning, I promise, I'm getting my job done. I just... I don't feel quite right while I'm doing it. Is that... is that the kind of thing you're asking about? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Did these feelings start after a specific stressful event?

Well, um... I guess... I mean, I really don't want to sound ungrateful for the opportunity, because I'm definitely not. But about a month ago, they asked me to cover the senior analyst duties at work. I was actually really honored they trusted me with it, and I definitely don't want to make it seem like I can't handle the job, because I'm keeping up with everything just fine. 

But... well, I suppose that's when I really started noticing this... this up-and-down pattern. It kind of kicked in right after I took on those extra responsibilities. 

I hope it doesn't make me sound weak to admit that a change at work threw me off balance like that. It's pretty normal to get a little overwhelmed by new duties, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right context, I hope that answers what you were asking.
Outside of work, do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things?

Well, um... not really, no. I mean, I hope I'm not giving the impression that I'm just a bundle of nerves all the time. I really try to keep things in perspective, you know? 

Outside of the office, I try to just... leave work at work. I don't really sit around agonizing over things or letting my mind run wild with worries. I mean, everyone has little things they stress about, right? Like bills or whatever, but nothing out of the ordinary. I really try to stay pretty level-headed about my day-to-day life. I hope that's the kind of thing you were looking for? I'm not trying to hide anything, I just honestly don't feel like I'm an overly anxious person in general.
Have you been having trouble sleeping lately?

Well, um... sleep has been a little tricky lately, I guess. I mean, I don't want to make a big deal out of it, because I know everyone has a bad night here and there, and I really am trying my best to manage it. 

But... well, I've noticed I'm either waking up way too early, you know, just lying there thinking about all the client tickets I need to handle, and I just can't seem to drift off again. Or, on the flip side, I'll get what should be a full night's sleep, but I still wake up feeling completely worn out. 

I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just complaining about being tired. I know the extra work is a privilege, and I'm pushing through it. It's just... the sleep thing is a bit frustrating. Is it normal to have your sleep thrown off like that when you're adjusting to new things? I hope I'm giving you the right details.
Before you took on the senior analyst duties a month ago, were you already having this heavy, low mood?

Well, um... I guess... I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I've just been dragging my feet for no reason or anything. I really try to stay positive and keep a good attitude, I promise I do. 

But, um... if I'm being completely honest, and looking back on it... I suppose those really low periods, where I just feel sort of heavy and, I don't know, guilty about everything... they didn't just start with the new duties. I've kind of been dealing with them off and on for, gosh, maybe about eleven months now? 

I hope you don't think less of me for not just snapping out of it sooner. I really have been trying to push through and not let it affect my work or the people around me. I just thought it was something I could handle on my own, you know? Is it okay that I waited this long to bring it up? I just didn't want to be a bother or seem like I was making excuses.
